name: Afrikaans
script: Latin with extra letters: ê, ô, û, ë, ï and the article 'n; left to right
basis: Stellenbosch University Survival / Campus Afrikaans outcomes for the themes; common beginner practice for the grammar order
src: Stellenbosch University Language Centre: Survival Afrikaans 2021 outcomes (six learning outcomes, no grammar listed)
Stellenbosch University Language Centre: Campus Afrikaans 2026 course information (five themes, no grammar listed)
elon.io: Afrikaans grammar A1 learner path (a grammar website's path, not a course syllabus)
note: No syllabus with a grammar order was opened. The Stellenbosch pages give only themes in order (greetings, personal information, questions, social talk, in and around town); the elon.io path suggested the early grammar (die / 'n, plurals, pronouns, one present form, is / het, questions, nie … nie, numbers, diminutives). The full lesson order, the past tense, modal verbs, possession with se, adjectives and all titles are common course practice and my own judgment.
hardest: The throaty g, and v said as f and w said as v
Double negation: nie … nie, with the second nie at the end
Word order: verb second, and the main verb sent to the end after modals and het ge-
Vowel spellings and marks: ee, oo, ie, oe, ê, ô, ë

items: Vowels and spelling: ee, oo, ie, oe, and ê, ô, ë
Consonants: the throaty g, v said as f, w said as v
Greetings: Goeiemôre, Hoe gaan dit?, Totsiens
Introducing yourself: My naam is…, Ek kom van…
Saying 'you': jy and u, oom and tannie
Pronouns: ek, jy, hy, sy, ons, julle, hulle
Present tense: one form for all (ek werk, hulle werk)
is and het: to be and to have
Questions: wat, wie, waar, wanneer, hoe, and yes/no questions
Verb in second place: Vandag werk ek
Numbers and prices: Hoeveel kos dit?
Telling the time: Hoe laat is dit?, kwart oor
Days and daily routine: Maandag, Dinsdag
Object pronouns: my, jou, hom, haar
Possession: my, jou, and se (Jan se boek)
Modal verbs: wil, kan, moet, sal, with the verb at the end
Ordering food: Kan ek … kry, asseblief?
Adjectives before the noun: 'n mooi dag, 'n goeie boek
Past tense: het ge- (ek het gewerk)
